main_body: Orange-red autumn tree canopy (large blob) on a thin brown trunk
top_band: organic canopy: no separate flat top band; the canopy is a rounded leaf mass lit from the top (light orange clumps rows 2-8 at x=23) over darker lower clumps. Trunk is a vertical shaft rows 29-44.
evidence: Organic tree: a rounded canopy blob whose upper clumps are lighter and whose lower part is darker with shadow under the canopy edge, sitting on a vertical trunk with a base. It reads as a volumetric mass lit from above rather than a flat elevation, with no isometric side face. The contract for rigid top/front pieces fits organic canopies loosely, but the rounded volume with lit top and shaded underside is acceptable.

style.evidence: Measured facts: the candidate has only 10 distinct colours and a median of 5 colours per tile, against about 108 per tile and 427-567 colours in the references. The canopy has some clumped dithering in orange and red, but the palette is very small and the clumps are far less defined than the references' multi-green leaf clusters. The trunk is a flat brown shaft with a near-black navy outline (the neutral/near-black edge share is 28%) and has little bark detail or root flare, where the references have a flared, textured base with roots and branches visible inside the canopy. The piece looks thinner and flatter than the references, so it fails.
